newsitem.title: FRANCE: UIC to get cash injection, sees H2 loss.
newsitem.headline: UIC to get cash injection, sees H2 loss.

text.p: The imminent recapitalisation of GAN property financing unit Union Industrielle de Credit, to the tune of 800 million francs, will be a cash injection, chief exeucitve Pierre de Lauzun said on Tuesday.

The capital increase, subscribed to by GAN, which controls 96.6 percent of UIC, is principally designed to soak up UIC's first-half losses. UIC plans as major restructuring with the aim of returning to profitability in 1998.

De Lauzon told a news conference "the second half should be along the lines of the first-half trend" and further losses were expected. A source close to the company said the loss for the year would likely be in excess of one billion francs.
UIC shares, in which trading was suspended on the basis of the information released on Tuesday, stood at 57.50 francs at the opening.
GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, also head of the UIC superisory board, said GAN would have no difficulty dealing with its duties towards UIC.
"With the sale of control in (GAN-controlled bank) CIC and the sale of CTR, GAN has the means to cover the capital increase without liquidity problems," he said.

De Lauzon said he did not reckon fresh cash would be needed to cover second-half losses. The group is expected to unveil a restructuring plan soon but de Lauzon declined to comment on job losses. UIC employes about 560 people at the moment.

UIC, hit when the bottom fell out of the property market at the start of the 1990s, was recapitalised a first time by GAN in 1995 to the tune of around 2.993 billion francs, equivalent to UIC's net consolidated losses.
